items.description: Multi-file code panel with optional readOnly, owned line markers, onValidityChange and onMonacoReady, merging every Monaco marker owner into Problems; the lazy loader example injects inline YAML schemas and same-origin yaml workers under CSP. The open file can be controlled (activeFile, onActiveFileChange) and the heading level set (headingLevel). Optional readOnly prevents editor edits. markers accepts CodePanelMarker entries {id,owner,file,line,column?,endLine?,endColumn?,severity,message,source?}; each owner is reserved for its consumer diagnostics service. The Problems list merges problems, consumer markers, and Monaco model markers from every owner, including worker-backed YAML schema errors. onValidityChange(valid) fires only when errors cross zero (initially clean emits nothing); warnings do not invalidate. onMonacoReady(monaco) configures consumer services once per Monaco instance and may return cleanup. loader can configure monaco-yaml before mounting; the only supported YAML path is consumer-injected, with enableSchemaRequest:false and an inline schema. examples/diagnostics.tsx demonstrates a semantic-worker owner next to schema diagnostics. See packages/editor/README.md for the lazy Vite yaml.worker recipe, Monaco 0.57 compatibility alias, and CSP worker-src self blob: with same-origin scripts and assets. Supplying markers (including []), onMonacoReady or onValidityChange enables model-marker collection; readOnly controls editing independently. Omitting diagnostics extensions preserves the original supplied-problems-only view. No kit runtime dependency on monaco-yaml.

items.name: Credential disclosure dialog
items.description: Controlled disclosure for an existing credential. Set disclosure ({variant: stored | fresh, credentialId, expiresAt: caller-formatted ReactNode, secret}) only after a successful response; null renders nothing while pending or on failure. Clear disclosure, additionalSecrets and secret-bearing revealContent in onClose to drop every secret; a fresh secret requires a new successful response before showing it again. No pending/error state or internal secret retention. Stored values start masked; each null-to-value opening or changed credentialId/secret resets masking and copy feedback. Fresh values use a non-copyable CodeBlock with a kit CopyButton and a replacement warning, or a masked SecretField when maskFresh is set at session start. Optional additionalSecrets ({id, label, value}) are always masked and use independent toggles and serialized copy actions; ids must be non-empty, unique and not secret, with the first duplicate winning. Multi-secret groups announce label plus copiedLabel, or copiedAnnouncementFor(label); onCopy(id) never receives a value. Every secret and the optional revealContent slot have data-kit-redact. The session key includes additional ids and values. presentation is dialog by default or inline, fixed until the next opening: inline is a named section, never traps focus or handles Escape, and its warning is a non-live note. Surviving focus stays; removing the focused slot or session control focuses the popup or inline heading. Focused inline unmounts return focus through the same resolvers. Dismissed retained props stay hidden; clear and re-set or change a session value to reopen. Optional English defaults through en/es i18n for title, description, credentialIdLabel, expiryLabel, secretLabel, showLabel, hideLabel, copyLabel, copiedLabel, successAnnouncement, failureAnnouncement, warningTitle, warningText and closeLabel. Copy results are announced politely, including manual-selection fallback. Popup initial focus and focus trapping use Base UI; at close, resolveReturnFocus() is validated for connection, visibility, enabled state and focusability, then fallbackFocus(), then the original opener. Synthetic fixtures only; the default Stored preview is masked and the Fresh preview starts closed. Optional labels?: Partial<CredentialDisclosureDialogLabels> overrides built-in copy; explicit props and validation messages win, then labels, then I18nProvider (en/es). No provider preserves English; fixtures and caller content stay unchanged. Interactive preview: /preview.html?kind=block&id=credential-disclosure-dialog--labels.

items.name: Data table
items.description: Opt-in csvExport adds an Export menu: All rows in current sort order across pages (before grouping), Current page in grouped display order, Selected rows and Copy selected rows (also Ctrl/Cmd+C on non-editable table content without a document text selection). csvExport accepts fileName and scopes (rows/page/selected). The filename defaults to the slugged caption, or table.csv without a supplied caption. Visible exportable columns keep display order; exportValue overrides accessor (nullish results fall back), columns without either are omitted, and exportable=false opts out. Values stay raw: ISO dates, booleans, numbers and empty null cells. CSV includes a BOM; CSV and clipboard TSV both use shared toCsv formula protection for headers and values. Single selection exports selectedId; multiple selection resolves include/exclude models across loaded rows. onExport receives scope, exported column ids, selected ids, sort and opaque filters; while pending the trigger stays focusable and busy and repeat exports are ignored. Use onExport for large result sets, and handle errors in the callback. Server pagination requires onExport and labels All rows with rowCount; clipboard copying and its shortcut are unavailable in server mode because unloaded selections cannot be copied completely. See examples/csv-export.tsx for client, delegated server and single-row previews. Generic typed table: sortable headers with aria-sort, row selection with select-all and indeterminate by default (selectionMode="multiple"), selectionMode="none" to hide selection, column visibility menu, density toggle, row actions, loading and empty states, client-side sort and pagination, optional row groups (groupBy) with rowgroup header rows, counts, keyboard-accessible collapse buttons and group selection; column resize (pointer drag or a focusable role="separator" handle with arrow keys, min/max widths, controlled columnWidths), column pinning to either edge with sticky cells (column menu or pinnedColumns), row virtualization for large datasets (aria-rowcount/aria-rowindex, works with selection and grouping), inline cell editing (text, number and select editors; Enter/F2 to edit, Enter/Tab to commit, Escape to cancel, onCellEdit can reject with an inline error) and saved views (filters, sort, visible columns, widths, pinning and grouping) with a view switcher to save as, rename, delete and reset. Opt-in selectionMode="single" uses native radios in a labelled fieldset (never virtualized; client pagination defaults to false, and paginated=true or paginationMode="server" enables pagination). Single mode uses selectedId/onSelectedIdChange or defaultSelectedId; isRowDisabled skips unavailable rows and preserves a checked disabled choice without callbacks. Supply legend, aria-label or aria-labelledby for the group and getRowLabel for each radio (otherwise the first column labels it). selectionName is used verbatim and must be unique per page; omitted names use an instance-unique useId name, and duplicate supplied names or missing group labels warn in development. Tab enters once on the checked enabled row or first enabled row; arrows wrap and skip disabled rows, Space selects, Shift+Tab exits, and all-disabled groups have no tab stop. No select-all, group checkboxes, bulk actions or selection summary appear in single mode. Examples in examples/single-selection.tsx: an uncontrolled non-paginated list with legend="Available items" and a controlled versions table with legend="Available versions", selectedId="v2" and a checked disabled version. Opt-in paginationMode="server" accepts a controlled 1-based page, pageSize and required rowCount (known total), with onPageChange/onPageSizeChange requests. Supplied rows render in order without client sorting or slicing, and headers have no sort affordance. Single selection keeps its chosen id across pages. Off-page choices leave every visible radio unchecked and the first enabled radio is the tab stop; name the current choice in the legend. See examples/paginated-single-selection.tsx for client and server pagination. The footer stays visible for empty results, clamps stale pages for display without callbacks, and hides during loading. Page-size changes may also request a page to keep the first visible row on screen. The consumer owns fetching and reconciles stale pages. See examples/server-pagination.tsx for an items/total/page/pageSize envelope consumer that handles both callbacks. Multiple selection preserves ids from other server pages by default; preserveSelection=false restores page-only reporting, and client tables can opt in with preserveSelection=true. selectedIds remains supported. A controlled selectionModel takes precedence and uses { type: "include", ids: string[] } for selected ids or { type: "exclude", ids: string[] } for every match except those ids. bulkActions(ids, model) receives the full include list; in exclude mode ids contains enabled selections in the current rows and the model is authoritative. One-argument actions remain compatible. selectAllMatching defaults to false and offers a strip after the page is fully selected: client mode includes every enabled row, while server mode requires onSelectionModelChange and reports an exclude model. The same button becomes Clear selection without moving focus; clearing returns focus to the page checkbox, or to the table when the checkbox is hidden or unavailable. An exclude model resets through both callbacks when filters changes by JSON value; filters must include every narrowing input, including search text. Paging, page size and sorting preserve selection. An exclude action covers the matching result set at action time, including later-created rows; the consumer executes it. isRowDisabled disables multiple-selection checkboxes and page/group/all-matching toggles skip known disabled rows. Server counts use rowCount minus explicit excluded ids, including disabled ids on the page where Select all is activated. isRowDisabled cannot evaluate unloaded rows, so the server must enforce eligibility for the complete matching result set; return only eligible matches and their rowCount when counts must exclude all unavailable rows. hideSelectAll defaults to false and hides just the header checkbox, retaining an accessible Selection heading. See examples/client-selection.tsx for client preservation, disabled rows and select-all-matching, and examples/server-pagination.tsx for controlled models, cross-page actions and the preservation/header options.

items.name: Flow builder
items.description: FlowGraph<Kind> is {nodes,edges}; FlowGraphChange names the edit type and affected nodeIds/edgeIds. Optional onGraphChange(graph, change) reports each committed add, delete, move, connect or inspector update once, omitting selected, dragging and measured from nodes. Inspector updates report every value change: hosts persisting every call should debounce. Selection, measurement, panel resizing, rejected connections and run mode report nothing. Optional graph controls content: render the parent graph without applying edits locally, while selection, measured sizes and active drag positions stay internal by stable node id. nodes/edges remain initial values when uncontrolled. onRun keeps the canvas node objects. builderNodes and builderEdges expose the shared starter graph; cleanFlowGraph(graph) returns a graph without transient node fields for persistence. examples/ControlledGraph.tsx shows graph={graph} onGraphChange={setGraph}. Palette ids skip existing kind-n ids. Visual flow editor with optional nodeTypes for named handles (branch-arm, parallel and sequence examples), onConnectEdge for edge type/data mapping, isValidConnection and onConnectionRejected for rules, onConnect for accepted connections, validationIssues for node/flow problems, mode="run" for a read-only canvas, nodeStatus for live badges, and onNodeSelect for pointer/keyboard selection. Optional nodeTypes registers kit-owned {type, handles:[{id,kind,position?,label?}], render, decorations?} definitions (no React Flow NodeProps). Keep nodeTypes and its renderer definitions stable (module scope or useMemo) across nodeStatus updates: recreating the array rebuilds custom node components and remounts them, defeating per-node memoization. onConnectEdge({source,target,sourceType,targetType,sourceHandle,targetHandle}) returns {type,data}; examples/extensions.tsx maps branch arm-0 to {kind: "branch-arm", armIndex: 0}, parallel branch to {kind: "parallel"}, and sequence next to {kind: "sequence"}. isValidConnection returns true, false, or {code,nodeId?,message}; onConnectionRejected reports {code,nodeId,message} once (nodeId defaults to the source) so consumers can forward it into validationIssues and control its lifetime, while onConnect reports accepted connections only. validationIssues decorates nodes with an icon and accessible text; node issues select and focus their node, and flow issues have no node link. mode="run" removes the Run action, palette, inspector and graph mutation while keeping labelled keyboard-selectable nodes, pan/zoom, fit controls and the wide-screen minimap. nodeStatus maps node IDs to FlowTone badges (running, degraded, failed, paused, done, handoff, review); onNodeSelect(id) handles pointer and keyboard selection. RunFlowExample shows live updates with per-node memoization. FlowNode defaults to the built-in FlowNodeKind union; use FlowNode<string> (or a custom kind union) for custom graphs, inferred by FlowBuilder and WorkflowBuilderPage. Custom renderers use kit status overlays and issue decorations by default; set decorations:"consumer" when render owns them, using data.decoration with accessible text and icons (for example, render:({data}) => <NodeCard title={data.title} tone={data.decoration?.status} />). FlowCanvas showInteractiveControls=false retains zoom/fit without the editing toggle. Named handles are keyboard controls: Enter or Space starts or completes a connection in edit mode; handles are disabled in run mode.

items.name: Sign-in form
items.description: Email (default) or text identifier and password sign-in. Supports identifier (type, autoComplete, label, help/helpId, placeholder, minLength/maxLength), messages (identifierRequired/identifierInvalid/identifierTooShort/passwordRequired), and React 19 ref.focus. Examples: custom-fields, no-terms, unavailable, loading, submitting and error. No filtering, sorting, selection, create action, toolbar, virtualization, pinning or sticky region. Error takes precedence over loading, then empty and data; retry uses the current i18n locale. Error headings use h3 for either section heading level. DataTable does not forward aria-describedby; its named containing region can reference the note instead. Count-only recipe: use hasMore={false} for the visible count without a note. PageToolbar has no count prop; this block carries the count. No navigation or focusable elements. Every visible string is overridable through noun, summaryLabel, formatCount and truncationNote; ReactNode overrides must remain plain text without interactive or hidden content. The i18n provider supplies translated defaults; locale overrides number formatting. items.name: AgentSurface
items.description: Opt-in, placement-neutral renderer for allow-listed agent content. Accepts only A2UI v0.9 command envelopes (A2UI_VERSION). Pass an immutable messages log and a trusted catalog; append createSurface, updateComponents, updateDataModel and deleteSurface messages. Component records have id, component, optional children (child ids), and flat catalog properties; the root id is "root". Text/Heading/Badge use text; Text optionally accepts href; Heading accepts level 1–6. Card contains children; Stack accepts direction (row/column) and gap (0–12). Button uses label, optional disabled and action { name, context }; Input uses label, optional text value/disabled and only type text. Select uses label, options [{ value, label }], optional value/disabled; Checkbox uses label, optional checked/disabled. Alert uses title and optional text. { path: "/user/name" } reads a JSON Pointer; Input/Select value and Checkbox checked write back to that path. updateDataModel { surfaceId, path?, value } replaces the value at path (default: model root). Every default Button is a submit control: Enter in an Input can activate the first Button, so keep a safe primary action first and avoid destructive actions in that position. Buttons, keyboard activation and implicit form submission emit onAction { name, surfaceId, context } with the current bound values. Replacing the log replays it; keep existing message objects stable when appending. Runtime validation rejects unsupported versions, malformed JSON, prototype keys, cycles, shared children and excessive trees (256 nodes, depth 32, 32 surfaces). Missing child definitions may arrive later. Unknown components and invalid properties show a localized placeholder and report a deduplicated onError diagnostic. The visible, accessible agent-content frame cannot be relabelled by the agent. Deletion or version suppression of rendered content restores focus to the next surviving sibling control, the first focusable textarea in the document, or the labelled container. Place the chat composer as that first textarea or provide a focusable sibling after the renderer; another textarea can otherwise receive focus. defineAgentCatalog accepts trusted host wrappers { component, validate }; validate must return a fresh allow-list of known properties or null. Wrappers receive { props, children, onValueChange, onAction } and must assign explicit kit props. Never spread agent data into elements. Custom URL properties must have names ending in href, src or url (case-insensitive) to receive the Markdown safeUrl policy; text renders as React text nodes. Custom catalogs can reintroduce phishing and executable content: audit their wrappers and validators, never allow passwords, payments, file uploads, arbitrary markup or host-chrome styling. Transport, side-panel placement, v0.8 adapters and Markdown integration belong to consumers or future changes. The live example demonstrates every default entry, model patches, actions, rejection, deletion and reset.

items.name: ChatDemo
items.description: Reference composition of the chat pack: suggestions in the empty state, attachments (pick, paste or drop), a compact ModelPicker in the composer, a tool call, a streamed markdown reply with sources (TypingIndicator, caret), Stop, MessageFeedback (copy, regenerate, thumbs with reasons), and a resizable details panel. items.description: Full-height chat frame: scrollable thread with auto-scroll that respects scrolling up, a jump-to-latest button, a composer pinned below and an optional resizable side panel (artifact or details).

items.name: ChatMessage
items.description: One conversation turn for the roles user (end-aligned bubble), participant (another person, e.g. a teammate: start-aligned outlined bubble with their name and avatar via `author` / `avatarSrc`), assistant, system and tool: avatar, author, timestamp, body and hover/focus actions (copy, retry, thumbs feedback). While streaming it is aria-busy, hides its actions and shows a TypingIndicator ("Assistant is typing") until text arrives and a caret after streamed plain text; ChatAnnouncer announces start and end once instead of every token. Copy actions show common.copyFailed when clipboard access is denied or unavailable, with no success icon; successful copies keep their labels and reset after 1600ms. items.name: Checkbox
items.description: Checkbox with optional label and description, including the indeterminate state. CheckboxGroup shares state across several checkboxes (plain or bordered list layout) and supports a parent "select all" checkbox.

items.name: ChoiceCard
items.description: Cards as controls. ClickableCard: the whole card is one link or button (a stretched title, so there is a single focus target with a short name) with icon, description, meta and a chevron. SelectableCard inside SelectableCardGroup: option cards with radio (single) or checkbox (multiple) semantics on Base UI RadioGroup / CheckboxGroup, with a check indicator, title, description, meta and disabled state.

items.name: Citation
items.description: Numbered source references for grounded answers: an inline [n] marker that previews the source (title, host, snippet, link) on hover, focus + Enter or click, and CitationList, the numbered list of sources under a reply. Only http(s) URLs become links.

items.name: CodeBlock
items.description: Read-only code panel with optional whole-source grammars: install the optional peer with `pnpm add shiki`, then import `createShikiHighlighter` from `@gntik-ai/ui/code-highlight-shiki` and wrap blocks in `<CodeHighlighterProvider highlighter={highlighter}>`. Read-only code panel with a filename / language header, a copy button ("Copied" feedback plus a polite live announcement), optional line numbers, highlighted lines, a soft-wrap toggle and a max height. Default colouring is a minimal tokenizer for ts/tsx/js/json/bash/css that only uses contrast-safe text tokens; use CodeHighlighterProvider for whole-source grammars, or pass `highlight` for a per-line override. Code is the inline variant for running text. Keep the instance stable with useMemo or create it outside render. The adapter lazily loads YAML, Python, Go and SQL (yml/py/golang/postgresql aliases), using the JavaScript regex engine without WebAssembly. Other languages retain the built-in tokenizer; unavailable languages stay plain and warn once in development. Add grammars with `createShikiHighlighter({ languages: { toml: loadTomlGrammar } })`, as the live example demonstrates. Each async loader returns a Shiki LanguageInput and can also override a default grammar. Custom CodeHighlighter implementations return CodeToken[][] for the whole source or null, with optional load(language): Promise<boolean>; useCodeHighlighter reads the nearest provider. Provider tokens use tokenClass only; invalid text or line counts fall back to the built-in tokenizer. Use maxHeight for long files to keep the panel scrollable; tokenization still runs on the main thread and is memoised.

items.name: Collapsible
items.description: A single show/hide section: an inline toggle ("Advanced settings") or a full-width row in the Accordion family. The chevron rotates and the height animates. Compound parts: Collapsible, CollapsibleTrigger, CollapsiblePanel.

items.name: Combobox
items.description: Searchable select: typing filters the list. Single select (ComboboxInput) or multi-select with removable chips (ComboboxChipsInput), an announced empty state, and rich rows via ComboboxItem children. Async options (`loadOptions(query, { signal })`: debounced, stale requests aborted, announced loading and error states with a Retry row) and creatable (`onCreate(input)` adds a “Create …” row). Opt-in `virtualized` windows flat items arrays (including async, Create and Retry rows); grouped items and static children retain full rendering. ComboboxContent accepts itemHeight (fixed pixels), estimatedItemHeight (default 32) and overscan (default 4). Keyboard highlights stay mounted; filtering resets scroll and reopening reveals the selection. Find-in-page and screen-reader browse mode reach mounted rows only; keyboard navigation reaches all options. Optional variant: outline (default), filled (secondary surface), or ghost (transparent chrome). FieldVariantProvider supplies the default; explicit props win. Ghost is for obvious editing contexts such as an edit-mode row or toolbar. Alternate variants retain focus, invalid and forced-colors boundaries.

items.name: CommandPalette
items.description: ⌘K / Ctrl+K command palette: a modal dialog with a search input over grouped commands (icon, label, description, shortcut keys). Commands are data with an onSelect. Fuzzy-ish ranking (prefix, word start, substring, subsequence; keywords and descriptions count), recent items while the query is empty, an empty state and footer hints. useCommandPaletteShortcut() exposes the shortcut on its own.

items.name: ContextMenu
items.description: Menu that opens at the pointer on right click or long press, and from the keyboard with Shift+F10 or the ContextMenu key on the focused area. Uses the Menu item parts (icons, shortcuts, destructive tone, checkbox/radio items, groups, submenus).

items.name: CopyButton
items.description: Copies a string, or the result of a (possibly async) getter, to the clipboard. Icon form (with tooltip) or labelled form, a "Copied" success state that resets after 2 s, a polite announcement (through LiveAnnouncer when present) and a fallback to execCommand when the Clipboard API is missing. Optional failureLabel and failureAnnouncement override failure feedback; failurePoliteness changes the LiveAnnouncer failure priority (assertive by default). `copyToClipboard` is exported too.

items.name: CSPProvider
items.description: CSPProvider passes the app server nonce to Base UI and kit inline elements; useCSP exposes the settings for custom elements. Disable style elements to use static CSS.

items.name: CursorPagination
items.description: See the cursor-pager-footer block example for data-table paginated={false} with a consumer-owned token stack. Stateless Previous/Next navigation for consumer-owned cursor stacks, with no page numbers, ranges or invented totals. Supply a plain-text summary (null keeps it empty) or shownCount with required labels.shownSummary and labels.totalSummary; only a positive exact total uses totalSummary. A pageSizeOptions select requires pageSize, onPageSizeChange, labels.rowsPerPage and labels.rowsPerPageLabel. Flat previousLabel, nextLabel and ariaLabel override labels.previous, labels.next and labels.navLabel, then provider catalog defaults. loading and busy are aliases: rendered buttons stay focusable and aria-disabled with aria-busy, while the select stays enabled. loadingLabel defaults to the catalog; null keeps the summary during busy. One persistent polite status writes once per changed text; mount, empty text and unchanged commits do not announce. Removal of the focused control moves focus to Next, Previous, the select or the nav root, in that order, even while busy; focus elsewhere never moves.

items.name: DateField
items.description: Typed local date and date-time entry in Intl locale order. DateField and DateRangeField expose named spinbuttons, calendar/min/max/disabled-date validation, ISO or numeric locale paste, and hidden form values. Granularity adds hours, minutes or seconds; a 12-hour clock adds AM/PM. Two-digit years remain literal (26 means year 26); empty segments use the TimePicker placeholder. forceLeadingZeros pads supplied values; typed segments are padded. Works inside Field. DatePicker triggers remain read-only.

items.name: DatePicker
items.description: Date field with a focusable trigger ref: a read-only input with the Intl-formatted date that opens a Popover with a Calendar. DateRangePicker (alias DateRangeInput) adds presets — Today, Last 7 days, Last 30 days, This month, Last month, Custom — beside a two-month range calendar. Min/max, disabled dates, locale, sizes, invalid state; works inside Field. `withTime` adds a TimePicker under the calendar (date + time value, 12/24h, minute step), closed with Done. DatePicker and DateRangePicker accept ref on their input; calling focus leaves the popup closed. Both pickers support `clearable`, `onClear` and `clearLabel`: reset from the field button, Delete/Backspace, or the popup Clear action. Clearing closes the popup and restores field focus. `readOnly` prevents edits. DatePicker accepts `timeZone` (IANA, UTC or system), defaulting to I18nProvider then the browser; invalid names fall back to the browser. Calendar days, today, min/max, time segments and edits use that wall clock while values stay Date instants. isDateDisabled receives a local-midnight proxy of the zoned calendar day. DST gaps move forward and overlaps choose the earlier occurrence. Non-system zones appear in field text and time labels unless `hideTimeZone` is true. With time, hidden values include the wall time and UTC offset (and seconds with `withSeconds`); date-only values submit YYYY-MM-DD and emit zoned midnight. Custom formatOptions retain their format but use the effective zone. DatePickerUtc demonstrates UTC, seconds, hidden zone labels and a provider-inherited date-only zone; DateRangePicker is unchanged. Optional variant: outline (default), filled (secondary surface), or ghost (transparent chrome). FieldVariantProvider supplies the default; explicit props win. Ghost is for obvious editing contexts such as an edit-mode row or toolbar. Alternate variants retain focus, invalid and forced-colors boundaries.

items.name: DateTimeRangePicker
items.description: Time range field for logs and metrics: quick presets (last 15 minutes, 1 hour, 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days, custom), a relative "Last N minutes/hours/days" mode and an absolute mode with a range Calendar plus start and end TimePickers, validated so the end is after the start. The value is serialisable: `{ mode: "relative", amount, unit }` or `{ mode: "absolute", start, end }`; `resolveTimeRange` turns it into instants. `timeZone` (IANA, UTC or system) defaults to I18nProvider then the browser; invalid names fall back to the browser. Absolute calendar days, today, min/max, time segments and edits use the zone, with compatible DST disambiguation (gaps move forward; overlaps choose the earlier instant). Non-system zones appear in the field text and start/end labels; `hideTimeZone` removes those labels. Relative presets remain instant-based and hidden start/end inputs remain ISO instants. DateTimeRangePickerUtc demonstrates UTC absolute editing and hidden zone labels.

items.name: Dialog
items.description: Modal window for focused tasks: forms, details, confirmations. Compound parts (Dialog, DialogTrigger, DialogContent, DialogHeader, DialogTitle, DialogDescription, DialogBody, DialogFooter, DialogClose) in four sizes. Named stacking layers keep nested popups, toasts and tooltips above the modal; see LayeredOverlays.

items.name: DiffViewer
items.description: Compares two texts, or two JSON values pretty-printed with sorted keys, line by line (Myers diff, no dependencies). Split or unified layout with a switch, line numbers, added/removed tints plus +/− markers and screen-reader text (never colour alone), word-level highlights inside paired lines, long unchanged runs collapsed behind "Expand N lines", +/− stats and optional file or version labels. The pure `diffLines`, `diffWords`, `diffJson` and `stableStringify` are exported.

items.name: DownloadButton
items.description: Saves required data (a string, Blob, or sync/async getter) as fileName. mimeType defaults to the Blob type, otherwise text/plain;charset=utf-8; extensions are not inferred. Inherits Button props, with a Download icon and translated default label. Async getters use Button loading, stay focusable and ignore repeat activation. onDownloaded fires after saving; onDownloadError receives failures, announced politely through LiveAnnouncer or a local status region. The static CSV, async success/failure and one-time JSON examples demonstrate these states and callbacks. downloadFile(data, fileName, mimeType?) is also exported; it removes the temporary anchor, revokes its URL on the next task, and does nothing without object URL support. Browsers differ: iOS Safari may open a tab. Exports are held in memory; use a server export for very large row sets. toCsv(rows, columns, options?) accepts columns with header and value (a row key or getter). Defaults: comma delimiter, header true, BOM false, CRLF, escapeFormulas true. Options also accept semicolon or tab delimiters, header false, BOM true, LF and escapeFormulas false. Null/undefined become empty cells, Dates use ISO, numbers/booleans retain their values and objects use JSON. Text starting with =, +, -, @, TAB or CR gets an apostrophe before CSV quoting; legitimate + or - text also changes. Disabling escapeFormulas is unsafe for spreadsheets. escapeCsvCell(text, delimiter?) always protects formulas and quotes delimiters, double quotes, CR and LF. It shares a name with the templates package helper: import explicitly from @gntik-ai/ui. Its CR-led cells are deliberately quoted, unlike the legacy audit-log helper.

items.name: Drawer
items.description: Panel that slides in from the right, left or bottom edge for details, edit forms and navigation. Fixed header and footer, scrollable body, swipe to dismiss. Under RTL (I18nProvider) `right` and `left` mirror to the inline end and start. Parts: Drawer, DrawerTrigger, DrawerContent, DrawerHeader, DrawerTitle, DrawerDescription, DrawerBody, DrawerFooter, DrawerClose.

items.name: EmptyState
items.description: Placeholder for an empty list, table or page: a neutral icon halo, a title, a short explanation and primary / secondary actions. Three sizes and an optional dashed border.

items.name: Field
items.description: Accessible form field scaffolding: Field, FieldLabel, FieldDescription, FieldError and FieldItem wire ids and aria-describedby for any kit control; Fieldset and FieldsetLegend group related fields under one name.

items.name: Grid
items.description: Responsive CSS grid. `cols` takes 1–12 or a per-breakpoint object ({ base, sm, md, lg, xl }) mapped to static classes; `minChildWidth` auto-fills as many columns as fit. GridItem spans columns (also responsive, or `full`). Gap on the spacing scale.

items.name: HoverCard
items.description: Rich preview of a link destination — a member, project or resource — shown on hover or keyboard focus after a short delay. Parts: HoverCard, HoverCardTrigger (a real link), HoverCardContent. The preview is supplementary: never put the only copy of an action or fact inside it.

items.name: InfoTip
items.description: Inline "i" help button that opens a small popover with an explanation, next to a form label, a stat or a table header. Named "More information about {label}"; works with click, keyboard and (optionally) hover, so the help is never hover-only.

items.name: Input
items.description: Single-line text input in two sizes (sm, md) with optional leading/trailing icons and addons (prefixes, units, keyboard hints, icon buttons). Invalid, disabled and read-only states; works inside Field. Opt-in `clearable` adds a labelled reset button; `clearOnEscape` consumes Escape only while the editable input has text. `onClear` runs after the value change and `clearLabel` overrides the localized name. Optional variant: outline (default), filled (secondary surface), or ghost (transparent chrome). FieldVariantProvider supplies the default; explicit props win. Ghost is for obvious editing contexts such as an edit-mode row or toolbar. Alternate variants retain focus, invalid and forced-colors boundaries.

items.name: JsonViewer
items.description: Collapsible JSON inspector built on TreeList: objects and arrays expand, values use contrast-safe type tokens, `search` highlights matches and expands their ancestors, `maxDepth` caps nesting, and a toolbar copies the selected node path or value. Optional `maxDisplayChars` (finite integer >= 1) measures UTF-16 units: strings as-is, other values as two-space JSON. Over-cap values become read-only text with an ellipsis (dropping a trailing high surrogate) and a warning Badge labelled by `labels.truncated`. Search has no effect in this fallback; Copy value copies the full measured text, as explained by `labels.copyFullHint`, and Copy path is disabled. `maxHeight` bounds the scrollable body. Only in capped mode, null, undefined and empty strings show `emptyContent` (default a muted dash). Leaving the cap unset preserves existing behavior. The cap limits rendering, not serialization cost. Built-in labels follow I18nProvider (en/es); caller overrides take precedence. See the TransferList catalog defaults example for a live Spanish preview of this component.

items.name: KanbanBoard
items.description: Columns of cards you reorder within a column and move across columns by pointer drag or keyboard. Controlled (`columns` + `onMove`, with `moveKanbanCard` to apply a move); every pick-up, move, drop and cancel is announced through a LiveAnnouncer. Built on the dependency-free `useSortable` hook (pointer + keyboard, press-and-hold on touch). Cards lift with a border and shadow only; nothing animates under reduced motion. Density-aware card padding (`size: "auto"`).

items.name: Kbd
items.description: Keyboard key chip (<kbd>) for shortcuts and hints, in three sizes. Use mod in Kbd or KbdCombo for ⌘ on macOS/iOS and Ctrl elsewhere; explicit keys stay unchanged. Symbol keys and Ctrl are announced by name, unless label overrides the spoken name. useOs() reports the detected OS (undetermined during SSR); getOs() detects it outside React. Both and the Os type are exported from @gntik-ai/ui.

items.name: KeyValueEditor
items.description: Editable list of key/value rows (environment variables, headers, labels): add and remove rows (no reordering), per-row validation (required key, key pattern, duplicate keys, optional required value and a custom `validate`), secret rows whose values are masked with a reveal toggle, bulk paste of `.env` text (comments ignored, existing keys updated) and "Copy as .env". Controlled (`value` + `onChange`) or uncontrolled. `parseEnv`, `serializeEnv`, `validateKeyValueRows` and `createKeyValueRow` are exported.

items.name: Lightbox
items.description: Full-screen image and video viewer: previous / next, zoom (buttons, keys or double click) with a scrollable stage, captions, a thumbnail strip and an announced position. Modal: focus is trapped, Escape closes and focus returns to the opener. Built-in labels follow I18nProvider (en/es); caller overrides take precedence. See the TransferList catalog defaults example for a live Spanish preview of this component.

items.name: Link
items.description: Styled anchor in brand green, underlined by default so inline links do not rely on colour (WCAG 1.4.1); standalone links (nav, cards, actions) pass underline="hover" or "none". `external` adds the external icon, a hidden "opens in a new tab" hint and safe rel/target. LinkProvider supplies the app router link so internal links navigate client-side; `render` swaps the element per link.

items.name: ListInput
items.description: Repeatable key/value rows for environment variables, headers or labels: add, remove and reorder (buttons or Alt+Arrow), paste `KEY=value` lines to bulk-add, per-row validation with duplicate-key detection, optional masked values with a reveal toggle. Changes are announced. Use ListInput for standalone pairs without a form library; use FieldArray from @gntik-ai/ui/forms for arbitrary object fields managed by react-hook-form. Built-in labels follow I18nProvider (en/es); caller overrides take precedence. See the TransferList catalog defaults example for a live Spanish preview of this component.

items.name: LiveAnnouncer
items.description: Screen-reader announcements for changes with no visible text: a polite (role="status") and an assertive aria-live region, plus `useAnnounce()` for any component below it. Used by KanbanBoard for pick-up / move / drop / cancel. Outside a LiveAnnouncer, `useAnnounce()` is a no-op.

items.name: Markdown
items.description: Safe, token-styled Markdown with GFM, code copying and streaming fence repair. Raw HTML stays skipped by default and URL attributes always pass safeUrl, including plugin-created URLs and component overrides. components merges over kit renderers; codeRenderers matches languages case-insensitively and receives code, language, streaming and complete (false only for the repaired fence). customTags allowlists standalone block tags: children use the same Markdown pipeline, attributes exclude on* and style, and unclosed tags render only while streaming. Unknown or malformed tags stay in the normal skipped-HTML pipeline without consuming later prose. useMarkdownContext exposes streaming to every renderer. Keep component maps and plugin arrays stable to preserve memoisation. User remarkPlugins follow GFM; user rehypePlugins follow kit HTML processing. Overrides and plugins are trusted executable code receiving untrusted content: validate data, render React text/children, and never use dangerouslySetInnerHTML. allowHtml lazily imports rehype-raw and rehype-sanitize; until loaded, HTML stays skipped. Its fixed subset is b, strong, i, em, u, s, del, sub, sup, kbd, mark, abbr[title], br, details[open] and summary. Other raw elements unwrap to text; scripts, styles, frames, embeds, forms, media, SVG, MathML, template and textarea drop their contents. Event handlers and style attributes are removed. MarkdownCustom demonstrates overrides, chart fences, think tags, both plugin types, opt-in HTML and partial streaming. Copy actions show common.copyFailed when clipboard access fails; successful copies reset after 1600ms.

items.name: MegaMenu
items.description: Top navigation with wide panels: items with sections open a panel of link columns with descriptions and optional featured content; plain items are links. Hover or click opens, the panel resizes between items, router links come from LinkProvider and the current page is marked. Use it as the StackedLayout sub-nav row; `megaMenuNavItems` feeds MobileNav. Built-in labels follow I18nProvider (en/es); caller overrides take precedence. See the TransferList catalog defaults example for a live Spanish preview of this component.

items.name: Menu
items.description: Dropdown list of actions or options: items with icon, shortcut hint and destructive tone, checkbox and radio items, labelled groups, separators and submenus. MoreMenu is the row-actions shorthand (icon button + items array).

items.name: MessageFeedback
items.description: Actions for an assistant reply: copy, regenerate and thumbs up / down toggles (aria-pressed). Thumbs down opens a popover with a reason picker and an optional comment. Controlled with `value` + `onFeedback`; pressing the active thumb clears it. A polite status confirms the feedback. Copy actions show common.copyFailed when clipboard access is denied or unavailable, with no success icon; successful copies keep their labels and reset after 1600ms. See the bilingual Result feedback live preview.

items.name: Meter
items.description: Usage meter for quotas and limits: label, value text, and a level set by thresholds (healthy → warning near the cap → destructive at or over it), with an optional note under the bar. `higherIsBetter` inverts the thresholds for scores and health (low = warning / destructive).

items.name: MobileNav
items.description: Small-screen navigation: a menu icon button opens a Drawer sheet (chrome surface) with the NavList groups and an optional footer slot. Activating an item closes the sheet; focus is trapped while open and returns to the button.

items.name: ModelPicker
items.description: Choose the model (and provider) for a conversation: options grouped by provider with a description, capability badges (vision, tools, reasoning, files, web, audio) and the context size; unavailable models stay listed, disabled, with the reason. `compact` gives a small borderless trigger for the ChatComposer toolbar. Controlled (`value` + `onValueChange`).

items.name: MultiSelect
items.description: Searchable multi-select: selected options as removable chips (extra ones collapse into "+N"), a "Select all" row, a clear button and rows with descriptions. Built on Base UI Combobox (multiple) with the Combobox house styles; works inside Field. Optional async options (`loadOptions`, debounced and abortable, with loading/error states) and creatable rows (`onCreate`). Opt-in virtualized renders only visible rows, with itemHeight, estimatedItemHeight (default 32) and overscan (default 4). Select all applies to the full enabled data set. Keyboard highlights stay mounted; find-in-page and browse mode reach rendered rows only. Built-in labels follow I18nProvider (en/es); caller overrides take precedence. See the TransferList catalog defaults example for a live Spanish preview of this component. Read-only mode preserves the selection and prevents edits. Optional variant: outline (default), filled (secondary surface), or ghost (transparent chrome). FieldVariantProvider supplies the default; explicit props win. Ghost is for obvious editing contexts such as an edit-mode row or toolbar. Alternate variants retain focus, invalid and forced-colors boundaries.

items.name: NavList
items.description: Vertical navigation for sidebars and settings pages: labelled (optionally foldable) groups of items with icon, label and badge, nested collapsible sub-items, and aria-current="page" on the active item with the brand accent bar. `collapsed` turns it into an icon rail with tooltips (nested sections open as flyout menus). Links render through LinkProvider, so client routers work.

items.name: NotificationsPopover
items.description: Bell icon button with an unread-count badge that opens a popover of notifications: title, body, relative time and a tone dot for unread items, a mark-all-read action, an optional footer (View all) and an empty state.

items.name: NumberInput
items.description: Numeric input with − / + steppers, a unit suffix, min/max/step clamping, locale formatting and an optional scrub label (drag to change). Sizes sm and md like Input; invalid, disabled and read-only states; works inside Field. Optional variant: outline (default), filled (secondary surface), or ghost (transparent chrome). FieldVariantProvider supplies the default; explicit props win. Ghost is for obvious editing contexts such as an edit-mode row or toolbar. Alternate variants retain focus, invalid and forced-colors boundaries.

items.name: OtpInput
items.description: One-time / verification code input: 4–8 character boxes, numeric or alphanumeric, optional group separator. Typing auto-advances, paste fills every slot, onComplete fires when full; invalid and disabled states; works inside Field.

items.name: OverflowList
items.description: Row of chips or avatars that renders items up to `max` (or to the available width with `responsive`, measured by ResizeObserver) and a "+N more" button that opens a Popover listing the rest. Built-in labels follow I18nProvider (en/es); caller overrides take precedence. See the TransferList catalog defaults example for a live Spanish preview of this component.

items.name: Pagination
items.description: Moves through pages of results. Pagination is numbered (first, last, siblings of the current page and ellipses, constant width) and page-size agnostic: page, pageCount, onPageChange. PaginationCompact is the table-footer form: "1–10 of 97" with previous/next.

items.name: PasswordInput
items.description: Password field on Input with a reveal toggle (aria-pressed) and an optional 4-segment strength meter. Strength comes from a small built-in heuristic or a `strength` prop (0–4); its text is linked to the input with aria-describedby. Works inside Field.

items.name: PeriodPicker
items.description: Whole ISO weeks, months, calendar quarters or years, single or range. PeriodPicker is a field and Base UI popover; PeriodCalendar is inline. Single values are the first day of a whole period at local midnight, not a single-day selection. Ranges include the last day of the final period. Weeks always run Monday–Sunday and use the ISO week-year, regardless of locale. Month names use Intl; quarter/week labels and presets use the en/es i18n catalogs. Form values: YYYY-MM, YYYY-Qn, YYYY or YYYY-Www; ranges submit <name>-start and <name>-end. Defaults are this and last complete period; presets=[] hides them. Min/max compare period overlap; disabled periods remain focusable. Range fields apply on the second pick; Escape discards an unfinished range. Calendar and DatePicker remain day-only.

items.name: PermissionMatrix
items.description: Roles (columns) × permissions (rows grouped in sections) editor. Cells are tri-state — allowed, denied, inherited — shown with an icon and a word, never colour alone; inherited cells are dashed and can say what they resolve to. Read-only columns (e.g. owner) and per-cell disabled reasons in a tooltip; controlled `value` + `onChange`; one tab stop with grid arrow-key navigation.

items.name: Popover
items.description: Non-modal floating panel anchored to a trigger, for short forms, details and filters. Optional arrow, four sides, three paddings. Close the popover before opening a Dialog from it: the popover layer is above the modal layer. Parts: Popover, PopoverTrigger, PopoverContent, PopoverTitle, PopoverDescription, PopoverClose.

items.name: PowerSearch
items.description: Structured filter input: pick a field, an operator and a value from suggestions (or type `status=failed`, `cost>100`), add free text, and edit committed terms from the keyboard. Emits a typed query AST (`{ type: "and", terms }`) with parse / format / match helpers; fields, operators and values are props.

items.name: Progress
items.description: Progress bar for a running task: optional label and formatted value, four tones (primary, success, warning, destructive), three heights, and an indeterminate state (value null) that stops pulsing under reduced motion.

items.name: QueryBuilder
items.description: Visual filter editor: nested AND/OR groups of field / operator / value conditions. Typed fields (text, number, enum, date, boolean) offer their operators and value editor (Input, NumberInput, Select / MultiSelect, DatePicker, ranges for "between"); add and remove conditions and groups up to `maxDepth`. The value is a serialisable tree; `queryToString(tree)` makes it human-readable and `evaluateQuery(tree, record)` tests a record. Inverted numeric or date "between" ranges show an inline error and are ignored by evaluation. Before sending a query to a backend, check each condition with `isConditionComplete` and `isConditionValid`; validation preserves the entered values.

items.name: RadioGroup
items.description: Single choice from a short list. RadioGroup + Radio with optional label, description and trailing content per option, in plain, list (bordered rows) and card variants.

items.name: Resizable
items.description: Split layouts with draggable dividers: ResizablePanelGroup (horizontal or vertical), ResizablePanel (default / min / max size in %, collapsible) and ResizeHandle (optional grip). Pointer drag and full keyboard support; the layout can be remembered in localStorage with `autoSaveId`. No extra dependencies.

items.name: ScheduleInput
items.description: Cron schedule editor: presets (hourly at minute, daily at, weekly on days at, monthly on day at) that write a 5-field cron expression, plus a raw cron field (*, lists, ranges, steps, names, macros) with validation and an error message, a plain-language summary ("Every weekday at 09:00") and the next runs in a time zone. Pure helpers: parseCron, describeCron, nextRuns. Display timeZone defaults to I18nProvider (system when unset); use the same zone on server and client. The TimeZone example shows the provider default and UTC overrides

items.name: ScrollArea
items.description: Native scroll container with thin token-styled scrollbars that fade in on hover and while scrolling. Vertical, horizontal or both; optional bordered surface. With an aria-label the viewport is a named region, and it joins the Tab order whenever it overflows.

items.name: SecretField
items.description: A secret value (API key, token, connection string) on Input: masked by default (fixed-length mask, optional visible prefix/suffix), a reveal toggle (aria-pressed), a CopyButton that copies the real value and announces it, an optional Rotate action behind an AlertDialog confirmation, and optional created / last-used meta. Optional showLabel, hideLabel, copyLabel and copiedAnnouncement override i18n defaults. Read-only by default (`editable` turns it into a password field). While masked and read-only the secret is not in the DOM, and it is never put in a title or tooltip. `maskSecret` is exported too.

items.name: Section
items.description: A painted content region (<section>, named by its title). Variants plain / card / muted, padding none–lg, optional dividers between children, and a header slot with title, description and actions.

items.name: Select
items.description: Pick one value from a short list in a popup, with SimpleSelect ref and triggerRef aliases for its trigger button. Compound parts (Select, SelectLabel, SelectTrigger, SelectContent, SelectItem, SelectGroup, SelectGroupLabel, SelectSeparator) plus a one-line SimpleSelect. Three trigger sizes; rich rows (avatar, status dot) via item children. SimpleSelect can load its options on first open (`loadOptions(query, { signal })`) with announced loading, empty and error states. Creatable lives in Combobox / MultiSelect (a select has no text input). SimpleSelect `clearable` adds a sibling reset button; Delete or Backspace on its trigger clears to null and retains focus. `onClear` runs after the value change; `clearLabel` overrides the localized name. For long lists, use Combobox with virtualized and a flat items array (see ComboboxVirtualized); Select requires its options to stay mounted for typeahead. Optional variant: outline (default), filled (secondary surface), or ghost (transparent chrome). FieldVariantProvider supplies the default; explicit props win. Ghost is for obvious editing contexts such as an edit-mode row or toolbar. Alternate variants retain focus, invalid and forced-colors boundaries.

items.name: Separator
items.description: Thin rule between content. Horizontal or vertical, default / subtle / strong weight, and an optional label (plain text, mono kicker or pill) placed at the start, centre or end of a horizontal line.

items.name: Skeleton
items.description: Loading placeholder in the shape of the content: block, text (one or more lines, the last shorter) or circle. Pulses gently and stops under prefers-reduced-motion. Decorative; announce loading on the container.

items.name: Slider
items.description: Pick a number or a range on a track. Single or range thumbs (one per value), optional visible label and live value readout, two sizes, works inside Field and Form.

items.name: Sparkline
items.description: Inline trend in pure SVG (no chart library): line or bars, optional area fill and min / max / last markers, fixed width and height. Coloured with token classes (stroke-primary, fill-primary/14…) so it follows the theme, and exposed as role="img" with a generated summary ("Requests: trending up 12% from 140 to 157…").

items.name: Spinner
items.description: Indeterminate loading indicator that inherits the current text colour.

items.name: SplitButton
items.description: A primary action joined to a menu of secondary actions. Two real buttons in a role="group": the action, and a chevron menu button (aria-haspopup="menu", aria-expanded) that opens the kit Menu. Takes Button's variants and sizes (`auto` follows the density), `actions` for a simple list or `menu` for custom MenuItems.

items.name: Stack
items.description: Flex layout primitives: Stack (any direction), HStack, VStack and Center. Gap on the spacing scale (0–12), align, justify, wrap and inline; render as any block tag with `as`, or any element with `render`. Paints nothing.

items.name: StatusDot
items.description: State dot with an optional label and a soft pulse for live states (disabled under reduced motion). Tones: success, warning, destructive, info, neutral, primary — generic, with no product-specific states. Without a label it needs an aria-label (exposed as an image) so colour is never the only signal.

items.name: StatusTag
items.description: State pill with a dot (running, queued, paused, failed, draft…). The state → tone mapping is a prop-driven dictionary merged over generic defaults, so products add their own states without touching the component.

items.name: Stepper
items.description: Wizard progress as an ordered list of steps (complete · current · upcoming · error), horizontal or vertical, with optional descriptions. Completed steps can be made clickable to go back; `compact` collapses it to "Step 2 of 5" with a thin bar. The current step carries aria-current="step".

items.name: SuggestionChips
items.description: Prompt suggestions: a two-column grid of cards with descriptions for an empty conversation, or a row of pills for follow-ups after a reply. Choosing one calls onSelect with its prompt.

items.name: Switch
items.description: On/off setting that applies immediately. Three sizes, optional inline label, works inside Field and Form.

items.name: Table
items.description: Styled semantic table parts: Table, TableHeader, TableBody, TableFooter, TableRow (selected state), TableHead (optional sort button with aria-sort), TableCell and TableCaption. Compact or comfortable density and an optional sticky header.

items.name: Tabs
items.description: Switches between views of the same block without leaving the page. Two variants (underline, pills), optional icons and count badges, a sliding indicator and a full-width layout. Compound parts: Tabs, TabsList, TabsTab, TabsIndicator, TabsPanel.

items.name: Terminal
items.description: Streamed command output (build, deploy, job logs). ANSI SGR colours map to contrast-safe tokens (`parseAnsi` is exported), `\r` progress lines rewrite in place, and a line cap drops the oldest output. It follows the tail until the user scrolls up, then offers “Jump to latest” with the count of new lines. Optional line numbers and timestamps, a wrap toggle, copy all and search with highlighted matches. The output is a `role="log"` with aria-live off unless `live` opts in. Stream through the `ref` handle (`write`, `writeln`, `clear`) or pass `lines`.

items.name: Text
items.description: Named type roles for body copy, labels, captions and headings on the brand scale. Text uses text-body, text-label, text-supporting, text-caption and text-display; code stays relative at 0.92em within its parent. Heading sizes display, xl, lg, md, sm, xs and 2xs use text-display and text-heading-* independently of semantic level 1–6 (level 2 defaults to text-heading-lg). Eleven roles come from typography.css, also exported as DTCG typography, Figma type/* variables and typeScale with pixel dimensions and unitless leading. font-*, leading-* and tracking-* utilities override role defaults; body, supporting and caption inherit weight and tracking. A font-size className such as text-[32px] replaces the entire role, including its leading, weight and tracking: unlike the previous separate variant classes, those defaults no longer remain. Supply explicit utilities when needed, for example text-[32px] font-bold tracking-tight for display, text-[12px] font-medium leading-tight for label, or text-[16px] font-semibold tracking-tight leading-snug for Heading. items.name: Textarea

Opt-in `clearable` reserves space for a reset button and returns focus to the textarea. `onClear` runs after the value change; `clearLabel` overrides the localized name. Optional variant: outline (default), filled (secondary surface), or ghost (transparent chrome). FieldVariantProvider supplies the default; explicit props win. Ghost is for obvious editing contexts such as an edit-mode row or toolbar. Alternate variants retain focus, invalid and forced-colors boundaries.

items.name: ThemeProvider

items.name: ThemeSwitcher

items.name: Thumbnail

items.name: TimePicker

Opt-in `clearable` resets every segment to its placeholder and focuses hours. `onClear` runs after emitting null; `clearLabel` overrides the localized button name. Accepts a Date, ISO string or epoch ms. Relative labels refresh on an adaptive interval that is cleared on unmount. With no heading, `title` remains required and renders as today. Supply either title or a non-empty heading, never both; the slot must contain exactly one h1. Pass titleRef to PageHeader (or a ref and tabIndex=-1 to a generic h1) and call ref.current.focus() on route load when needed. Keep slot links and actions empty so the primary action stays first in main’s Tab order. Use page for a dedicated flow, fullscreen for a focused in-page flow, or the dialog-wizard block (default "dialog") for a compact create flow. Closing never resets the consumer-controlled current step or data. Exit, Escape and Cancel on step zero use confirmExit (default true). Outside presses are ignored unless closeOnInteractOutside is true, then use the same exit confirmation. returnFocusRef overrides focus return to the opener. Each step focuses its heading, first control or body, then announces via a separate polite live region. Supply stepAnnouncement({position,total,label}) from your i18n (required for rich step labels); positions are one-based. All action labels, stepsSummaryLabel and pendingLabel are overridable with i18n fallbacks. finishPending or nextLoading disables Finish and shows pendingLabel in overlay mode. stepsInteractive defaults to true; false omits onStepClick so completed steps are display-only. stepStatusText and formatStepCount pass through to both Stepper variants for localized status words and position text. backDisabled locks Back using aria-disabled while keeping it focusable, including on step zero; it cannot activate Cancel. items.name: Create wizard
items.description:
Focus-mode create flow on WizardLayout. Without flowSteps, the existing details, source, configuration and editable review flow, CreateWizardProps, copy and defaults are unchanged. Page mode is the default; mode="overlay" keeps the parent list mounted without a route change. Overlay size defaults to fullscreen; size="dialog" uses a popup (fullscreen on mobile). Legacy closing preserves answers; confirming exit in flow mode resets answers and the current step.

## Caller-defined flow mode

Import CreateWizardPage (or CreateWizardFlow) and CreateWizardFlowProps<V> from @gntik-ai/templates. flowSteps selects the additive generic variant; legacy-only props (steps, copy, sources, regions, title, stepFeedback, onStepChange) cannot mix with it. V is the caller's object type. The kit owns current step, values and validation visibility. The display-only Stepper follows the supplied order and appends review. Zero caller steps renders review directly.

| Prop | Type / behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| flowSteps | readonly { id: string; label: string; readOnly?: boolean; render({ values, setValue, errors }): ReactNode; validate?(values): { fieldErrors?, blocking? } }[]; ids must be unique and stable |
| initialValues | V; used at mount and restored on confirmed exit |
| summary | (values: V) => readonly { stepId: string; label: string; value?: string or null }[] |
| labels | Required CreateWizardFlowLabels; no template-owned visible or accessible copy has a fallback |
| onFinish | (values: V, { signal: AbortSignal }) => void or Promise<unknown>; one signal per attempt |
| onExit | Called once after confirmed exit, after reset and abort; Stay calls nothing |
| onComplete | Uncontrolled only; (result: unknown) => void, once after success is committed and announced |
| submitState | Controlled when provided at mount: {status:'idle'}, {status:'submitting'}, {status:'success', result?:unknown}, or {status:'error', error?:unknown, message?:string} |
| resourceHref | (result: unknown) => string or undefined; only called with a non-null success result |
| errorMessage | (error: unknown) => string or undefined; empty text uses labels.errorFallback |
| confirmExit | Defaults to true; Exit, Escape and overlay Cancel open confirmation. false exits directly |
| mode, size, open, onOpenChange, description, returnFocusRef, closeOnInteractOutside | WizardLayout presentation props; closing itself is not confirmation or reset |

labels supplies title, exit, cancel, back, next, finish, pending, review (Stepper label), reviewTitle (heading), edit(stepLabel), emptyValue, success(result), errorFallback, openResource, exitTitle, exitDescription, exitConfirm, exitCancel, steps (Stepper name), stepsSummary, skipLink, stepStatusText (complete/current/upcoming/error), formatStepCount(position,total) and stepAnnouncement({position,total,label}). Positions are one-based. Step labels, validation messages, summary labels/values and rendered body content also belong to the caller's namespace. Every DescriptionListCard receives the owning step label as its explicit title, labels.edit(stepLabel), explicit items and an empty description. All steps get a card, even with no matching rows; empty values use labels.emptyValue.

## Validation and navigation

validate runs on every render, including caller re-renders (for example members.count quota changes). A non-empty blocking message disables Next immediately. It is visible as ordinary text and announced politely once per new value, including entry and one frame after overlay opening. Clearing blocking re-enables Next without a press. fieldErrors is Partial<Record<keyof V,string>>. Errors become visible after the first Next press on their step and remain live thereafter. With errors, Next does not advance and focuses the first aria-invalid="true" field. Render fields using Field invalid, FieldLabel, Input and FieldError to associate errors and controls. Blocking does not hide visible field errors. A readOnly step must render its fixed value as text, without editable controls; only its blocking result gates Next and its fieldErrors are ignored. Back, Next and review Edit preserve values. Edit returns to the owning step and focuses its heading. No direct Stepper jumps are available.

## Submit ownership and aborts

In uncontrolled mode, Finish shows labels.pending in both presentations. Resolve commits success, announces labels.success(result) politely, then calls onComplete(result) once. Reject keeps values and review, renders errorMessage(error) or labels.errorFallback, announces assertively and re-enables Finish. Identical repeated failures each announce; changing settled error text announces once, unchanged text does not. Visible success, error and blocking text is never a live region. All announcements use useAnnounce from the nearest LiveAnnouncer; the template provides one only when needed. Put LiveAnnouncer at page level when onComplete closes/unmounts the flow, so the message survives.

Controlled mode renders submitState only. Each enabled Finish press calls the existing onFinish once; its returned result never changes kit state and onComplete is never called. The caller must pass through submitting for every attempt, discard completions when signal.aborted, and reset submitState to idle in onExit before reopening. Switching between controlled and uncontrolled after mount is unsupported. AbortSignal is a cancellation contract, not a transport: callers must honor it. Confirmed exit and unmount abort the current attempt. Uncontrolled aborted settlements cannot update state, announce or complete, including an older attempt settling after reopening.

While submitting or after success, Back has backDisabled (aria-disabled but focusable), review cards have no Edit, and Finish is loading or disabled. Exit remains enabled. Pending Finish and locked Back retain focus. A focused control becoming disabled or removed sends focus on success to the resource link, or to the success heading (tabIndex=-1) if no result/href exists; in all other cases it goes to the current heading. Focus never moves to a live region. Page Back/Next preserve focus unless the pressed control becomes disabled. Overlay step changes focus the new heading and announce via LiveAnnouncer. Escape in a portalled Select or Menu stays local.

## Examples

examples/Invite.tsx is a generic single-recipient invite with a read-only workspace context, one email checked against /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/, a members.count quota, exactly Owner/Admin/Member roles, and an optional message with maxLength=500. Its copy is one English page namespace. examples/labels.ts lists every required label. UncontrolledPending, UncontrolledSuccess and UncontrolledError cover a never-settling attempt, a success resource link and a failure fallback. ControlledIdle, ControlledSubmitting, ControlledSuccess and ControlledError show each caller-owned state. Every example has a create-wizard--<kebab-name> preview entry; Invite uses create-wizard--invite. The three-theme browser axe loop visits each step, review, submit state and exit confirmation. examples/Overlay.tsx retains the original list-to-overlay project flow with step-local error and empty surfaces.

A controlled caller's onFinish can use this pattern (with its own transport, values and state): setSubmitState({status:'submitting'}); try { const result = await save(values, {signal}); if (!signal.aborted) setSubmitState({status:'success',result}); } catch (error) { if (!signal.aborted) setSubmitState({status:'error',error}); }. onExit resets to idle before reopening. Keep the page-level LiveAnnouncer mounted when closing.

All flow surfaces reuse kit components and existing tokens; no new CSS variables. Themes: dark, light and high_contrast.

| Prop | Type | Default / behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| title | string | Live event stream; PageHeader h1 |
| description | string | Subscribe to a source and inspect the events it emits. |
| form | ReactNode | Non-sensitive Source field inside FormSection; sensitive fields must use the kit PasswordInput |
| status | idle / connecting / live / error / stopped | idle; fully controlled |
| events | LiveEvent[] | Empty fixture; unique id, timestamp, type, optional summary and unknown payload; oldest first |
| maxEvents | number | 500; nonnegative integer; retains newest entries, evicts oldest; invalid values use 500 |
| eventTypes | string[] | created, updated, deleted; multiple ToggleGroup, initially all enabled; unlisted types remain visible |
| countAnnouncement | string | Omitted; optional count text throttled by the consumer, never inferred from events.length |
| onSubscribe | () => void | Subscribe callback in idle, stopped and error; disabled while connecting |
| onStop | () => void | Stop callback while live |
| onSelectEvent | (event: LiveEvent) => void | Mouse or keyboard selection callback |
| error | string | Generic subscription error; ErrorPanel shown when status=error, inside role=alert |
| validationMessage | string | Omitted; destructive InlineCallout |
| shell | Omit<ConsoleShellProps, 'children'> | ConsoleShell fixture defaults; explicit consumer navigation, workspace, user and topbar slots |

Status mapping: idle = neutral Not subscribed; connecting = info Connecting with pulse; live = success Live with pulse; error = destructive Error; stopped = warning Stopped. Subscribe is shown in idle/connecting/error/stopped and is disabled for connecting; live shows Stop. Idle has No events yet, live-empty has Listening for events, connecting replaces the log with decorative skeletons, and stopped keeps supplied buffered events visible.

## ARIA pattern

PageHeader h1 and labelled FormSection. One polite atomic live region announces connection status and explicit consumer-throttled count text only. LogViewer uses announceLines=false: role=log and aria-live=off; event additions are silent. Connecting uses an aria-busy section. Stream errors use ErrorPanel inside role=alert; validation uses InlineCallout. Inspect buttons have the name Inspect event <timestamp> and aria-pressed. InspectorLayout owns the complementary landmark on desktop, Drawer on small screens, docking, pinning and focus return. Pinning does not freeze the payload: subsequent selection updates it; eviction preserves the last inspected payload with the note This event is no longer in the buffer.

## Keyboard table

| Key | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Form fields, Subscribe/Stop, filters, search, Follow, row inspect/copy and panel controls |
| Enter / Space | Activate buttons; select an event; toggle Follow and pinning |
| Arrow keys | Navigate ToggleGroups and the JsonViewer tree |
| Escape | From unpinned panel or toggle, close and return focus to inspector toggle; pinned panel ignores Escape, Close panel closes it |

Follow pins the bottom, where the newest row is added. Scrolling up by more than one row turns Follow off and preserves the viewport offset; switching Follow on returns to the bottom.

## Themes and examples

Dark (default), light and high_contrast use only kit tokens. Connecting/live pulses stop under prefers-reduced-motion. State previews: live-event-stream--connecting, --live-empty, --live-with-events, --error and --stopped. Every state and the default template are covered by axe in all three themes.

items.name: Public hub
items.description:
Unauthenticated entry hub on AuthLayout full-bleed with PageHeader, explanatory cards and navigation actions. Use public-hub instead of landing for an account entry point without a marketing hero or screenshot; use sign-in-card for a single sign-in form. Recommend 2 to 4 cards; any number is supported. Cards use the kit sm breakpoint: one column below sm, two from sm. ARIA: a section labelled by the text span inside the single PageHeader h1, h2 card headings and a ul/li card list. The title span owns the aria-labelledby target id in server HTML and after hydration; PageHeader has no heading-id prop. Loading replaces content with decorative kit Skeletons in an aria-busy section named by loadingLabel. Keyboard: Tab and Shift+Tab move through the primary, secondary and tertiary links in visual order; Enter follows href and invokes onClick, with visible focus and no trap. AuthLayout retains its skip link, named "Skip to main content", before the content in both states. The PageHeader title inherits truncation for long titles.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default / behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| eyebrow | string | Omitted; optional Badge before PageHeader |
| title | string | Welcome; PageHeader h1 |
| description | string | Omitted; PageHeader description |
| cards | { title: string; body: string }[] | Omitted; explanatory list with h2 headings |
| primaryAction | { label: string; href: string; onClick?: MouseEventHandler<HTMLAnchorElement> } | Sign in, #sign-in; Button rendered as an anchor |
| secondaryAction | Same action shape | Omitted; secondary Button rendered as an anchor |
| tertiaryLink | Same action shape | Omitted; one kit Link |
| footer | string | Omitted; Separator then supporting Text |
| loading | boolean | false; replaces header, cards and actions; hides eyebrow/footer copy |
| logo | ReactNode | Active preset logo from AuthLayout |
| loadingLabel | string | Loading; accessible name of the busy section |

Optional content has no default fixtures and creates no empty wrappers; an empty cards array also renders no list. Without footer there is no separator. Preview fixtures: public-hub--full, public-hub--minimal, public-hub--loading and public-hub--minimal-loading.

items.name: Flow builder
items.description: onSave(graph) receives the graph on screen (controlled graph, latest reported edit, or initial starter graph), without selected, dragging or measured node fields. Zero-argument handlers remain valid. Optional graph and onGraphChange pass through to FlowBuilder. Committed edits show actionBar.unsaved, a resolved save shows actionBar.saved, and a rejected save retains unsaved status and releases loading. Edits during a pending save remain unsaved. examples/SaveGraph.tsx shows a controlled graph and onSave={(graph) => localStorage.setItem("workflow-builder-example", JSON.stringify(graph))}; hosts own persistence. Full-screen workflow editor with optional nodeTypes, onConnectEdge, onConnect, isValidConnection, onConnectionRejected, validationIssues, mode="run", nodeStatus and onNodeSelect passed to FlowBuilder; codePanel passes readOnly, markers, onValidityChange, onMonacoReady and loader to an optional CodePanel (branch, parallel, sequence and worker-backed YAML examples). The app must import '@gntik-ai/flow/styles.css' once for the canvas styles. Optional nodeTypes, onConnectEdge, onConnect, isValidConnection, onConnectionRejected, validationIssues, mode, nodeStatus and onNodeSelect pass to FlowBuilder unchanged (see its branch, parallel and sequence examples). mode="run" hides Save, Publish and the saved notice, and preserves focus and node selection. Optional codePanel renders a companion CodePanel and passes all its extensions: readOnly, markers, onValidityChange, onMonacoReady and loader; run mode forces its readOnly to true. For example, WorkflowBuilderPage mode="run" nodeStatus={{step:"running"}} onNodeSelect={openDetails}; codePanel={{files,problems:[],loader:yamlLoader,markers}} uses consumer-owned same-origin YAML workers and inline schemas.
